_comment: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and the two GLM-5.3 checkpoints on the 8x A40 box (46068 MiB / 44.99 GiB each, 359.9 GiB total). Every path, file size, GGUF architecture id and quantization below was read off the files on that host, and every Hugging Face revision is the commit hash the local download recorded in .cache/huggingface/download/*.metadata (each matches the repo's current main as of 2026-09-11). Three registry facts decide how this matrix is driven. (1) MULTI-GPU PLACEMENT IS NOT THE SAME FOR THESE TWO FAMILIES, and that is what `min_tp` and the two backend columns encode. glm-dsa / glm5next run in a native whole-model executor that claims EVERY visible GPU and places whole layers on them when no `--tp` is passed (GlmDsaModel.Native.cs: nGpu = TS_GLM_NGPU ?? (tp > 1 ? tp : 0), where 0 means every visible GPU, and the native loader then places whole layers), so `ggml_cuda_layer` - no `--tp`, no CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES - is how a 236 GiB GLM checkpoint is served here, and it is the only placement in which GLM-5.3's NextN block loads. qwen4exp does NOT work that way: its layer split comes from the SHARED loader, which reads the split degree from `--tp N` (ModelBase.ResolveTensorParallelSupport sets LayerSplitDegree only when tpDegree > 1; TENSORSHARP_TP_DEGREE defaults to 1 = no splitting), so without `--tp` TensorSharp puts all 175.3 GiB on one 44.99 GiB card and the load fails. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next therefore declares `min_tp` and runs on the `ggml_cuda_tp` column; its `--tp 8` cells are still a LAYER split, announced by the loader. (2) The llama.cpp build on this host (/workspace/llama.cpp, ggml 0.23.0) implements `qwen4exp` and `glm-dsa` but has no `glm5next` at all - not the arch enum, not a model graph - so the llama.cpp column cannot run glm53-flash. `defaults.engines` is therefore TensorSharp only; add the reference column explicitly for the two models that have one. (3) No benchmark media is staged on this host (/workspace/bench_media does not exist), so the `image` scenario is declared but left out of `defaults.scenarios`; stage an image at paths.media.image (or set BENCH_IMAGE) before running `--scenarios image`. Nothing here carries a measured throughput number: no run has been made against these three models, and no claim below rests on one.

media._note: Not present on this host yet - stage the files or point these env vars elsewhere before running a multimodal scenario. A missing file is a hard error in the request builder (scenarios._data_uri), not a silently text-only request.

qwen38-flash-next._gguf_note: general.architecture = qwen4exp, general.name = 'Qwen3.8 Flash Next', size_label 512x56B, general.file_type = 7 (Q8_0), 48 blocks, 512 experts top-10, context_length 262144. The local files are byte-identical in size to the repo's Q8_0/ directory: 10,946,624 + 682,434,912 + 54,400,261,312 + 49,446,841,216 + 49,668,930,400 + 34,015,618,784 = 188,225,033,248 bytes (175.3 GiB) across six shards. The local directory is flat while the repo keeps one subdirectory per quant, which is why the gguf entry carries an explicit `url`.
qwen38-flash-next._modalities_note: text + image only, and image only because the mmproj was checked: mmproj-BF16.gguf (907,542,944 bytes) declares clip.has_vision_encoder = true with projector_type qwen3vl_merger and NO clip.has_audio_encoder, and the trunk GGUF carries qwen4exp.ple.image_token_id = 248056. Nothing in either file describes an audio or video decoder, so neither modality is claimed. The `image` scenario has not been run against this model here; what is verified is that the file declares the tower and that Qwen4ExpModel implements IVisionCapableModel.
qwen38-flash-next._mtp_note: No MTP/NextN draft head: a scan of all six shards found 1,224 tensors and not one `nextn`/`mtp` name, and qwen4exp declares no nextn_predict_layers. Qwen 3.8's NextN ships as a SEPARATE GGUF that SpeculativeDraftHeadLoader cannot attach to this architecture, so no `mtp_draft` is registered either - `--mtp on` cells are gated out with a reason instead of quietly serving standard decode.
qwen38-flash-next._tp_note: THIS MODEL NEEDS `--tp N`, and that is what `min_tp` above is for. Qwen4ExpArchitecture declares MultiGpu = MultiGpuMode.LayerSplit, which means the SHARED loader spreads it - and the shared loader only spreads when a degree is given: ModelBase.ResolveTensorParallelSupport sets LayerSplitDegree = tpDegree only for tpDegree > 1, and at degree 1 ModelBase builds a single-device GGML context. So `--tp 8` here is an 8-way LAYER split (the loader prints 'Multi-GPU: 8 GPUs by LAYER SPLIT ...' and the model still loads with TpDegree 1), while no `--tp` at all is one GPU and an OOM. That buys capacity, not decode speed. It is the same and only multi-GPU mode llama.cpp offers qwen4exp, which is why the `ggml_cuda_tp` column tells llama.cpp to split by layer rather than by tensor - the two engines are then doing the same thing and the column is comparable. Run it with: --models qwen38-flash-next --backends ggml_cuda_tp (tp_degrees already carries 8).
qwen38-flash-next._llamacpp_note: llama.cpp on its own would host this model at tp=1 - its default `-sm layer` spreads it over every visible GPU, which is why the checkpoint is not out of reach for the reference column. `min_tp` is nevertheless a MODEL-level gate in config.py and is applied to every engine, so the llamacpp cells at tp=1 are skipped with the same reason as the TensorSharp ones. Take the reference column on ggml_cuda_tp instead, where this config tells llama.cpp `--split-mode layer` over the same eight GPUs that TensorSharp's `--tp 8` layer-splits across: `--engines tensorsharp,llamacpp --models qwen38-flash-next --backends ggml_cuda_tp`.
qwen38-flash-next._vram_note: Weights alone are 175.3 GiB against 44.99 GiB per A40. `min_tp` is 4 because that is the arithmetic floor for the WEIGHTS (175.3 / 44.99 = 3.90) - it is not a claim that 4 works: at tp=4 the layer split leaves ~1 GiB per card for the KV cache, activations and the vision tower, so the intended degree on this box is 8 (21.9 GiB of weights per card). Degrees between the two are untested here; the tp=1 cell is gated out rather than left to OOM.

glm53-flash._gguf_note: general.architecture = glm5next, general.name = 'GLM 5.3 Flash', size_label 288x10B, general.file_type = 10 (Q2_K; UD-Q2_K_XL is mixed - blk.45 alone holds Q2_K, Q3_K, Q5_K, Q6_K and Q8_0 tensors), 46 blocks (45 trunk + 1 NextN), 288 experts top-8, context_length 1048576, NoPE MLA (rope.dimension_count = 0). Local sizes match the repo's UD-Q2_K_XL/ directory exactly: 9,429,859 + 49,294,975,936 + 49,949,266,048 + 9,466,399,584 = 108,720,071,427 bytes (101.3 GiB) across four shards. The repo keeps the shards in a per-quant subdirectory and the mmproj at the root, hence the explicit `url` on the gguf entry only.
glm53-flash._modalities_note: text + image. mmproj-BF16.gguf (1,164,010,080 bytes) declares clip.has_vision_encoder = true with projector_type glm5next (24 blocks, 448px, patch 14) and no audio encoder, so image is the only extra modality claimed. GlmDsaModel.LoadVisionEncoder accepts an mmproj for glm5next only (it warns and ignores one on glm-dsa), which is why the sibling glm53 entry carries none.
glm53-flash._mtp_note: The checkpoint DOES carry a NextN block (glm5next.nextn_predict_layers = 1, and blk.45 holds nextn.eh_proj / enorm / hnorm / shared_head_norm plus a complete MLA + 288-expert layer), but TensorSharp cannot engage it: the native executor refuses glm5next speculation outright in ggml_ops_glm_dsa.cpp ('[glm] glm5next NextN/MTP speculation is not implemented; serving standard decode'). No claim is made about llama.cpp here - the build on this host has no glm5next graph at all. Registered false so `--mtp on` is gated with a reason rather than reported as a speculative run that silently decoded normally.
glm53-flash._llamacpp_note: This host's llama.cpp has no glm5next support at all - `glm5next` appears nowhere in its sources and src/models/ has glm-dsa.cpp but no glm5next graph - so llamacpp cells for this model would fail at load. config.py has no per-model engine restriction, so nothing gates them: run this model with `--engines tensorsharp` (the default).
glm53-flash._tp_note: Runs at tp=1, i.e. with NO `--tp`, which is not the same statement as 'one GPU': the native glm executor enumerates every visible GPU and places whole layers on them when no degree is given. `--tp N` on this family means TRUE tensor parallelism (a different placement, not more capacity), which is what the ggml_cuda_tp column is for; it has not been run here.
glm53-flash._vram_note: 101.3 GiB of weights against 44.99 GiB per A40: at least three GPUs before KV, and the no-`--tp` layer split uses all eight. `min_tp` stays 1 because in THIS config tp=1 pins no devices (defaults.tp_devices is empty) and the native executor then takes every GPU - see the tp_devices note below.

glm53._download_note: The download is complete: all seven shards are present with no .incomplete parts, the fetch logged 'exit=0 repo=unsloth/GLM-5.3-GGUF pattern=UD-Q2_K_XL/*', and every local size matches the repo's UD-Q2_K_XL/ listing byte for byte.
glm53._gguf_note: general.architecture = glm-dsa, general.name = 'Glm-5.3', general.version = 5.3, size_label 256x22B, general.file_type = 10 (Q2_K, mixed within UD-Q2_K_XL), 79 blocks (78 trunk + 1 NextN), 256 experts top-8, MLA with 64 query heads and 1 KV head, DSA indexer 32 heads, context_length 1048576, rope base 8e6 - the same block shape GLM-5.2 has, which is why it loads on the existing glm-dsa path unchanged. Sizes: 9,428,677 + 49,172,427,136 + 49,091,626,976 + 49,091,626,976 + 49,091,626,976 + 49,994,703,552 + 7,426,966,496 = 253,878,406,789 bytes (236.4 GiB) across seven shards.
glm53._modalities_note: Text only, and verified rather than inferred from the name: the full file listing of unsloth/GLM-5.3-GGUF at the pinned revision contains no mmproj of any kind (the Flash repo has two). There is no vision tower to point `--mmproj` at, and GlmDsaModel would refuse one on glm-dsa anyway.
glm53._mtp_note: The NextN block is present and complete - glm-dsa.nextn_predict_layers = 1 and blk.78 carries nextn.eh_proj/enorm/hnorm/shared_head_norm alongside a full MLA + 256-expert MoE layer - which is exactly what the native loader checks before paging it in. IT ONLY LOADS WITHOUT `--tp`. blk.78 ships no nextn.shared_head_head.weight, so the draft block borrows the trunk's LM head, and ggml_ops_glm_dsa.cpp refuses to draft from a column-parallel head whenever tp > 1 ('[glm] the NextN block has no LM head of its own and the trunk head is column-parallel under --tp N; serving standard decode'). An `--mtp on` cell is therefore only truthful on the ggml_cuda_layer backend, which passes no `--tp`; on ggml_cuda_tp at tp > 1 it would report mtp=on over a run that decoded normally, and the harness has no per-backend MTP gate to stop it. VERIFY IT IN THE SERVER LOG, and verify the right line: the benchmark runs the NATIVE executor (--backend ggml_cuda), whose load banner reads '[glm] glm-dsa: 78 trunk layers +1 NextN/MTP draft block, ...' when the block is in and '... 78 trunk layers (NextN block present but not loaded; --spec loads it)' when it is not. The managed per-op path's 'NextN/MTP draft head ready (block 78, ...)' line is NOT printed on this backend.
glm53._tp_note: Runs at tp=1, i.e. with NO `--tp`: the native glm executor takes every visible GPU and places whole layers on them, which is the only way 236.4 GiB is served on eight 44.99 GiB cards, and the only way the NextN block loads. `--tp N` on glm-dsa means TRUE tensor parallelism - a different placement with a different failure mode (GLM-5.2 at `--tp 2` on 3x97 GiB needed 116 GiB/rank and failed the load outright), and it disables MTP. Nothing at tp > 1 has been run for this checkpoint here.
glm53._vram_note: 236.4 GiB of weights against 44.99 GiB per A40 needs at least six GPUs before KV; the no-`--tp` layer split uses all eight, which is the only configuration with headroom on this box.

text_long.description: Long-context single-turn text prompt (~2k-token context preamble + passage)

multi_turn.description: 3-turn conversation (~2k-token context preamble), timed on the final turn

image.description: Image understanding through the model's own mmproj (qwen38-flash-next, glm53-flash); needs paths.media.image staged first

backends._comment: Two GPU columns, distinguished by whether a GPU COUNT is passed at all - which is the one thing these two architectures disagree about. ggml_cuda_layer passes no `--tp` and pins no devices: the glm native executor then claims every visible GPU and places whole layers on them, and llama.cpp does its own default layer split over the same eight, so the column is comparable for the GLM models. It is NOT a column qwen4exp can run on: the shared loader needs `--tp N` before it splits anything, so Qwen3.8-Flash-Next declares min_tp and its cells here are recorded as skips. ggml_cuda_tp is the column that passes `--tp N` (and, through config.tp_device_env, pins CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to the first N devices). What `--tp N` MEANS is per architecture and the loader announces it: qwen4exp gets an N-way layer split, glm-dsa gets true tensor parallelism. llama.cpp is told `--split-mode layer` on that column because layer placement is the only multi-GPU mode it has for qwen4exp (`-sm row` refuses to load it) - that keeps the qwen column engine-to-engine comparable, and it is why the GLMs should not be run on this column with both engines: TensorSharp would be tensor-parallel while llama.cpp was layer-split. No CPU column: all three are large MoE checkpoints and applies() skips cpu-kind backends for size_class large anyway.

ggml_cuda_layer.display: CUDA layer split (all visible GPUs, no --tp)
ggml_cuda_layer._env_note: Every key under `tensorsharp.env` is exported verbatim to the server process, so nothing but real variables belongs in it. MAX_CONTEXT is a per-sequence hard limit for both families (the glm native loader treats its own value as a ceiling only when MAX_CONTEXT is unset). KV_CACHE_DTYPE binds on the managed KV path, i.e. qwen4exp; the glm native executor allocates its KV as GGML_TYPE_F16 unconditionally, so f16 is stated here to keep the two families on one budget, not because the variable steers the GLM runs.

llama._comment: llama-server divides `-c` across its `--parallel` slots, so 262144 / 4 = 65536 per slot - the same per-sequence window the TensorSharp backends set with MAX_CONTEXT, against the same four concurrent sequences (TS_SCHED_MAX_RUNNING_SEQS). Both engines therefore size the same KV budget. All three models declare far more context (262144 for qwen4exp, 1048576 for both GLM checkpoints) than fits beside these weights; 65536 per sequence is a chosen ceiling, not a fitted one.

_ready_timeout_note: Ceilings, not measurements: /workspace is a MooseFS network filesystem and a cold load reads 101-236 GiB through it. ready_timeout_s itself takes only numbers - config.py floats every value in that block - so the note lives out here.

defaults._models_note: All three are listed so the matrix is complete, but the default backend can only host the two GLM checkpoints: qwen38-flash-next needs `--tp N` (see its _tp_note) and its default cells are recorded as skips reading 'needs --tp 4 (does not fit 1 GPU(s))'. Run it with: run_matrix.py --config benchmark_config_glm53_qwen38.json --models qwen38-flash-next --backends ggml_cuda_tp
defaults._scenarios_note: prefill_8k / prefill_32k are not declared in the `scenarios` block above on purpose: config.synth_scenario builds any `prefill_<N>` from the shared corpus, so they need no per-config declaration. `image` is declared but left out until media is staged on the host.
defaults._thinking_note: GLM-5.3's chat template reasons regardless of this flag (it always emits a reasoning turn), so a thinking=false row is not a no-reasoning row for the two GLM models.
defaults._tp_degrees_note: 1 and 8 because the two families need different launches and each degree is a skip on the column that cannot serve it: at tp=1 nothing is pinned and no `--tp` is passed (the GLMs' placement; qwen38 is gated out by min_tp), and at tp=8 the ggml_cuda_tp column passes `--tp 8` over all eight GPUs (qwen38's placement; the GLMs would switch to true tensor parallelism there, which is why that column is not a default). tp=8 cells on ggml_cuda_layer are skipped by applies() because that column declares no tensor-parallel mapping - a free skip, not a run.
defaults._tp_devices_note: Intentionally empty: config.tp_device_env() then sets no CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES at tp=1, so each engine sees all eight A40s - which is what makes the GLMs' no-`--tp` layer split cover the box. Filling this in would pin a tp=1 cell to GPU 0, where none of these three checkpoints fit. With the pool empty, a tp=N>1 cell still pins devices 0..N-1 (config.py's documented fallback), so `--tp 8` gets all eight.
